people.joram-israel.role: King of Israel whom Jehu kills
people.joram-israel.relations: Son of Ahab and Jezebel, and king after his brother Ahaziah. The text also calls him Jehoram.
people.joram-israel.meaning: He leads Israel, Judah, and Edom against Moab. Later he fights Syria and is wounded at Ramoth Gilead. Jehu shoots him at Jezreel and has his body thrown on Naboth’s land.
people.jehoram-judah.role: King of Judah, son of Jehoshaphat
people.jehoram-judah.relations: Son of Jehoshaphat and father of Ahaziah of Judah. He marries Ahab’s daughter and is also called Joram.
people.jehoram-judah.meaning: He rules Judah for eight years and follows the ways of Ahab’s house. Edom breaks away from Judah and sets up its own king. He attacks the Edomites by night, but Edom stays free. Libnah also breaks away.
people.mesha.role: King of Moab who rebels against Israel
people.mesha.relations: King of Moab. His oldest son was to be king after him.
people.mesha.meaning: He pays Israel lambs and wool, then rebels after Ahab dies. Three kings attack, and he cannot break through to the king of Edom. He offers his oldest son as a burnt offering on the wall. Great wrath comes against Israel, and the text does not say whose.
people.edom-king.role: Unnamed king who joins the war on Moab
people.edom-king.relations: He marches with the kings of Israel and Judah against Moab.
people.edom-king.meaning: He marches seven days with Israel and Judah, and the army runs out of water. He goes down with them to Elisha. Later Mesha tries to break through to him and fails.
people.mesha-son.role: Mesha’s oldest son, offered on the wall
people.mesha-son.relations: Oldest son of Mesha, king of Moab.
people.mesha-son.meaning: He was to rule Moab after his father. Mesha offers him as a burnt offering on the wall. The text gives him no name and no words.
people.oil-widow.role: Unnamed widow whose oil pays her debt
people.oil-widow.relations: Widow of one of the sons of the prophets. Mother of two sons.
people.oil-widow.meaning: She tells Elisha that a creditor is coming to take her two sons as slaves. She has only a pot of oil. She borrows containers, shuts the door, and pours until all are full. Elisha tells her to sell the oil, pay the debt, and live on the rest.
people.oil-sons.role: Unnamed sons who bring the containers
people.oil-sons.relations: Sons of the widow. A creditor comes to take them as slaves.
people.oil-sons.meaning: They bring empty containers to their mother while she pours oil. One son tells her that no container is left, and the oil stops. Elisha says the oil will pay the debt and feed the family.
people.shunammite-woman.role: Unnamed woman of Shunem who hosts Elisha
people.shunammite-woman.relations: Wife of an old man in Shunem. Mother of the son Elisha promises.
people.shunammite-woman.meaning: She feeds Elisha and has a room built for him on the roof. Elisha promises her a son, and the boy later dies on her knees. She rides to Mount Carmel and will not leave Elisha until he comes. Later the king gives back her house and land after seven years away.
people.shunammite-husband.role: Unnamed husband in the Shunem household
people.shunammite-husband.relations: Husband of the Shunammite woman and father of her son. Gehazi says he is old.
people.shunammite-husband.meaning: His wife asks him to help make a room for Elisha. His son cries out about his head in the field, and he sends him home. He asks why his wife is going to Elisha that day.
people.shunammite-son.relations: Son of the Shunammite woman and her husband.
people.shunammite-son.meaning: He is born as Elisha said. One day in the field his head hurts, and he dies at noon. Elisha prays and lies on him, and the boy sneezes seven times and wakes. In chapter 8 he stands with his mother before the king.
people.gehazi.role: Elisha’s servant who takes Naaman’s gifts
people.gehazi.relations: Servant of Elisha. He deals with the Shunammite woman, Naaman, and the king.
people.gehazi.meaning: He tells Elisha that the Shunammite woman has no son. He lays Elisha’s staff on the dead boy, and nothing happens. He lies to Naaman to get silver and clothes, and Naaman’s leprosy clings to him. Later he tells the king what Elisha has done.
people.baal-shalishah-donor.role: Unnamed man who brings first-fruit bread
people.baal-shalishah-donor.relations: He comes from Baal Shalishah and brings food to Elisha.
people.baal-shalishah-donor.meaning: He brings twenty barley loaves and fresh grain to Elisha. Elisha has it set before a hundred men. They eat, and some is left over.
people.naaman.role: Syrian army captain healed of leprosy
people.naaman.relations: He serves the king of Syria. A captive girl from Israel waits on his wife.
people.naaman.meaning: He is angry when Elisha only sends word to wash in the Jordan. His servants reason with him, so he dips seven times and is clean. He asks for two mule loads of earth. He says he will sacrifice only to the LORD.
people.naaman-wife.meaning: The captive girl tells her that the prophet in Samaria could heal Naaman. Someone carries the girl’s words to Naaman. The text says nothing more about her.
people.captive-girl.role: Unnamed girl taken from Israel in a raid
people.captive-girl.relations: She waits on Naaman’s wife in Syria.
people.captive-girl.meaning: Syrian raiders carry her away from the land of Israel. She tells her mistress that the prophet in Samaria could heal Naaman. Her words send Naaman to Israel, where he is healed.
people.elisha-dothan-servant.role: Unnamed servant who sees the chariots of fire
people.elisha-dothan-servant.relations: With Elisha when the Syrian army surrounds Dothan.
people.elisha-dothan-servant.meaning: He goes out early and sees an army around the city. He asks Elisha what they should do. Elisha prays, and he sees horses and chariots of fire on the mountain.
people.samaria-women.role: Unnamed women starving in besieged Samaria
people.samaria-women.relations: Two women of Samaria. One cries out to the king of Israel on the wall.
people.samaria-women.meaning: One woman says they agreed to eat their sons, one each day. They boiled and ate her son, and the other woman then hid hers. The king tears his clothes when he hears it. He swears to kill Elisha that day.
people.four-men.role: Four men with leprosy at Samaria’s gate
people.four-men.relations: They sit together at the gate of Samaria during the siege.
people.four-men.meaning: They choose to give themselves up to the Syrians and not starve. They find the camp empty, eat, and hide silver, gold, and clothing. Then they say it is a day of good news and tell the gatekeepers. The king sends men to check, and the people go out for food.
people.samaria-officer.role: Captain who doubts Elisha’s promise of food
people.samaria-officer.relations: The king leans on his hand. The king puts him in charge of the gate.
people.samaria-officer.meaning: He asks if such food could come even if the LORD made windows in heaven. Elisha says he will see it but not eat it. The next day the people trample him in the gate, and he dies.
people.ahaziah-judah.role: King of Judah killed by Jehu’s men
people.ahaziah-judah.relations: Son of Jehoram of Judah and Athaliah. Father of Joash of Judah and brother of Jehosheba.
people.ahaziah-judah.meaning: He rules Judah for one year and follows the ways of Ahab’s house. He goes to war with Joram and later visits him at Jezreel. Jehu’s men strike him in his chariot, and he dies at Megiddo. He is not Ahab’s son Ahaziah, the king of Israel in chapter 1.
people.athaliah.role: Mother of Ahaziah who takes Judah’s throne
people.athaliah.relations: Mother of Ahaziah of Judah. The text calls her the daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
people.athaliah.meaning: When her son dies, she kills the royal children and rules for six years. Jehosheba hides one child, Joash, from her. She hears him crowned, tears her clothes, and cries out that it is treason. The captains take her out of the LORD’s house and kill her.
people.jehu-messenger.role: Young prophet sent by Elisha to anoint Jehu
people.jehu-messenger.relations: One of the sons of the prophets. Elisha sends him to Jehu.
people.jehu-messenger.meaning: He finds Jehu among the captains at Ramoth Gilead and takes him inside. He pours oil on Jehu’s head and says the LORD makes him king. He tells Jehu to strike Ahab’s house. Then he opens the door and runs.
people.bidkar.role: Jehu’s captain who throws down Joram’s body
people.bidkar.relations: Jehu’s captain. He once rode with Jehu behind Ahab.
people.bidkar.meaning: Jehu tells him to throw Joram’s body onto Naboth’s field. Jehu reminds him of the LORD’s word against Ahab that they both heard. The text says nothing more about him.
people.jehonadab.role: Son of Rechab who rides with Jehu
people.jehonadab.relations: Son of Rechab. He meets Jehu on the road to Samaria.
people.jehonadab.meaning: Jehu asks if his heart is right, and he says it is. He gives Jehu his hand and rides in his chariot to Samaria. He goes with Jehu into the house of Baal before the worshipers are killed.
people.jehoahaz-israel.role: King of Israel crushed by Syria
people.jehoahaz-israel.relations: Son of Jehu. Father of Joash of Israel.
people.jehoahaz-israel.meaning: He rules Israel for seventeen years and follows the sins of Jeroboam. Hazael and Benhadad of Syria wear his army down to almost nothing. He begs the LORD, and the LORD gives Israel a savior. He is not Josiah’s son Jehoahaz in chapter 23.
people.jehosheba.role: King’s daughter who hides the child Joash
people.jehosheba.relations: Daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah of Judah.
people.jehosheba.meaning: Athaliah is killing the king’s sons. Jehosheba steals Joash away and hides him and his nurse in a bedroom. He stays hidden in the LORD’s house for six years. Chronicles also names her as Jehoiada’s wife.
people.joash-judah.role: Hidden child who becomes king of Judah
people.joash-judah.relations: Son of Ahaziah of Judah and Zibiah, and father of Amaziah. Also called Jehoash, and not Israel’s King Joash.
people.joash-judah.meaning: He is hidden for six years and crowned at seven. He tells the priests to repair the LORD’s house, but they do not. A chest then collects the money, and it goes straight to the workers. He sends the temple gold to Hazael, and later his servants kill him.
people.joash-nurse.role: Unnamed nurse hidden with the child Joash
people.joash-nurse.relations: Nurse of Joash of Judah. Jehosheba hides them both.
people.joash-nurse.meaning: Jehosheba puts her and Joash in a bedroom, out of Athaliah’s sight. The text says nothing more about her.
people.jehoiada.role: Priest who crowns Joash of Judah
people.jehoiada.relations: Priest in the LORD’s house. He teaches King Joash of Judah.
people.jehoiada.meaning: He shows the hidden king’s son to the captains and sets guards around him. He crowns Joash and orders Athaliah taken out and killed. He makes a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people. Later he sets a chest by the altar to collect repair money.
people.mattan-baal.role: Priest of Baal killed before his altars
people.mattan-baal.relations: Priest of Baal in the days of Athaliah and Joash of Judah.
people.mattan-baal.meaning: After Joash is crowned, the people break down the house of Baal. They kill Mattan in front of the altars. The text says nothing more about him.
people.jozacar.role: Servant who helps kill Joash of Judah
people.jozacar.meaning: He and Jehozabad strike King Joash of Judah, and Joash dies. Amaziah becomes king. Amaziah later kills the servants who killed his father.
people.jehozabad.role: Servant who helps kill Joash of Judah
people.jehozabad.meaning: He and Jozacar strike King Joash of Judah, and Joash dies. Amaziah later kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children.
people.amaziah.role: King of Judah beaten by Israel’s Joash
people.amaziah.relations: Son of Joash of Judah and Jehoaddin. Father of Azariah.
people.amaziah.meaning: He kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children. He beats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth Shemesh. Joash breaks down part of Jerusalem’s wall and takes the gold. Later men plot against Amaziah, and he is killed at Lachish.
people.zibiah.meaning: The text names her as the mother of Joash of Judah. She comes from Beersheba. It tells no story about her.
people.joash-israel.role: King of Israel who visits the dying Elisha
people.joash-israel.relations: Son of Jehoahaz of Israel and father of Jeroboam. Also called Jehoash, and not Judah’s King Joash.
people.joash-israel.meaning: He weeps over the dying Elisha, shoots an arrow, and strikes the ground three times. He then beats Benhadad three times and wins back Israel’s cities. He also beats Amaziah of Judah at Beth Shemesh and breaks Jerusalem’s wall.
people.ben-hadad-hazael.role: King of Syria who loses cities to Joash
people.ben-hadad-hazael.relations: Son of Hazael, and king of Syria after him.
people.ben-hadad-hazael.meaning: He and his father Hazael hold Israel down in the days of Jehoahaz. After Hazael dies, he rules Syria. Joash of Israel beats him three times and takes back the cities. He is not the earlier king of Syria whom Hazael served.
people.jeroboam-ii.role: King of Israel who wins back land
people.jeroboam-ii.relations: Son of Joash of Israel and father of Zechariah. He is usually called Jeroboam II.
people.jeroboam-ii.meaning: He rules Israel for forty-one years and keeps the sins of the first Jeroboam. He restores Israel’s border from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah. Jonah had spoken this word. The text says the LORD saved Israel by his hand.
people.jonah.role: Prophet whose word about the border comes true
people.jonah.relations: Son of Amittai, from Gath Hepher.
people.jonah.meaning: The LORD speaks through Jonah about Israel’s border. Jeroboam son of Joash then restores that border. This book tells nothing more about Jonah.
people.jehoaddan.relations: Mother of Amaziah, from Jerusalem. The text spells her name Jehoaddin.
people.jehoaddan.meaning: The text names her as Amaziah’s mother and says she is from Jerusalem. It tells no story about her.
people.zechariah-king.role: Last king of Israel from Jehu’s family
people.zechariah-king.relations: Son of Jeroboam son of Joash. Shallum kills him.
people.zechariah-king.meaning: He rules Israel for six months and keeps the sins of Jeroboam. Shallum strikes him down before the people and takes the throne. The LORD had told Jehu his sons would rule to the fourth generation. Zechariah is the last of them.
people.shallum-king.role: King of Israel for one month
people.shallum-king.meaning: He plots against Zechariah, kills him before the people, and rules in Samaria. After one month Menahem comes from Tirzah and kills him. He is not Shallum, the husband of Huldah, in chapter 22.
people.menahem.role: King of Israel who pays silver to Pul
people.menahem.meaning: He comes from Tirzah, kills Shallum, and takes the throne. He attacks Tiphsah because it would not open its gates. He gives Pul a thousand talents of silver to keep his throne. He takes fifty shekels from each rich man to pay it.
people.pekahiah.role: King of Israel killed by his captain
people.pekahiah.relations: Son of Menahem. His captain Pekah kills him.
people.pekahiah.meaning: He rules Israel for two years and keeps the sins of Jeroboam. Pekah and fifty men of Gilead attack him in the king’s house in Samaria. Pekah kills him and takes the throne.
people.urijah-priest.role: Priest who builds Ahaz’s new altar
people.urijah-priest.relations: Priest in Jerusalem under King Ahaz.
people.urijah-priest.meaning: Ahaz sends him a drawing of an altar he saw in Damascus. Urijah builds it before the king comes home. Ahaz then tells him to burn the daily offerings on the new altar. Urijah does all that Ahaz commands.
people.shalmaneser.role: King of Assyria who besieges Samaria
people.shalmaneser.relations: Hoshea of Israel serves him and pays him tribute.
people.shalmaneser.meaning: He comes against Hoshea, and Hoshea pays him tribute. In Hezekiah’s fourth year he besieges Samaria. The city falls after three years.
people.so-egypt.role: King of Egypt to whom Hoshea sends messengers
people.so-egypt.relations: Hoshea of Israel sends messengers to him.
people.so-egypt.meaning: Hoshea sends messengers to So and stops paying Assyria. The king of Assyria finds out and puts Hoshea in prison. The text does not say what So does.
people.tartan.meaning: The king of Assyria sends him from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army. He comes with Rabsaris and Rabshakeh, and only Rabshakeh speaks. The older manual treats Tartan as an official title.
people.rabsaris.meaning: The king of Assyria sends him from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army. He stands with Tartan and Rabshakeh by the upper pool. The text gives him no words.
people.abi.meaning: The text names her as Hezekiah’s mother and Zechariah’s daughter. It tells no story about her.
people.hephzibah.meaning: The text names her as Manasseh’s mother. It tells no story about her.
people.meshullemeth.relations: Daughter of Haruz of Jotbah. Mother of Amon.
people.meshullemeth.meaning: The text names her as Amon’s mother. Her father is Haruz of Jotbah. It tells no story about her.
people.amon-king.role: King of Judah killed by his servants
people.amon-king.meaning: He rules Judah for two years and serves the idols his father Manasseh served. His servants kill him in his own house. The people of the land kill those servants and make his son Josiah king.
people.hilkiah-priest.role: High priest who finds the book of the law
people.hilkiah-priest.relations: High priest under Josiah. He works with Shaphan the scribe.
people.hilkiah-priest.meaning: He finds the book of the law in the LORD’s house. He gives it to Shaphan. He goes with four others to ask Huldah about it. Later Josiah has him bring out the vessels made for Baal.
people.shaphan.role: Scribe who reads the book to Josiah
people.shaphan.relations: Son of Azaliah. Father of Ahikam and grandfather of Gedaliah.
people.shaphan.meaning: Josiah sends him to Hilkiah about the repair money. Hilkiah gives him the book of the law, and he reads it. He reads it again before the king, and Josiah tears his clothes. He then goes with the others to Huldah.
people.huldah.role: Prophetess who answers Josiah about the book
people.huldah.relations: Wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe. She lives in Jerusalem, in the second quarter.
people.huldah.meaning: Josiah’s five men come to her with the king’s question. She says the LORD will bring on Jerusalem all the evil in the book. She says Josiah humbled himself, so he will not see it. The men carry her answer back to the king.
people.shallum-huldah.meaning: The text names him as Huldah’s husband and keeper of the wardrobe. It tells no story about him. He is not Shallum, the king of Israel in chapter 15.
people.ahikam.role: One of five men sent to Huldah
people.ahikam.meaning: Josiah sends him with four others to ask the LORD about the book. They go to Huldah and bring her answer back. Later his son Gedaliah is made governor of Judah.
people.achbor.role: One of five men sent to Huldah
people.achbor.meaning: Josiah sends him with four others to ask the LORD about the book. They go to Huldah and bring her answer back to the king.
people.asaiah.meaning: He hears Josiah’s order after the book is read. He goes with four others to Huldah, and they bring back her answer.
people.jedidah.relations: Daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath. Mother of Josiah.
people.jedidah.meaning: The text names her as Josiah’s mother. Her father is Adaiah of Bozkath. It tells no story about her.
people.joshua-governor.role: Governor of the city, named for a gate
people.joshua-governor.relations: A gate of the city bears his name.
people.joshua-governor.meaning: Josiah breaks down the high places at the entrance of Joshua’s gate. The text names Joshua only to mark that gate. It tells no story about him.
people.jehoahaz-judah.role: Josiah’s son, king for three months
people.jehoahaz-judah.meaning: The people of the land anoint him king after Josiah dies. He rules three months. Pharaoh Necoh binds him at Riblah and takes him to Egypt, where he dies. He is not Jehu’s son Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
people.hamutal.role: Mother of two later kings of Judah
people.hamutal.meaning: The text names her as mother of two kings, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah. Her father is Jeremiah of Libnah. It tells no story about her.
people.zebidah.relations: Daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah. Mother of Jehoiakim.
people.zebidah.meaning: The text names her as Jehoiakim’s mother. Her father is Pedaiah of Rumah. It tells no story about her.
people.nehushta.relations: Daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. Mother of Jehoiachin.
people.nehushta.meaning: She goes out with her son Jehoiachin to the king of Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar carries her to Babylon with the king, his wives, and his officers.
people.seraiah-priest.role: Chief priest put to death at Riblah
people.seraiah-priest.relations: Taken with Zephaniah the second priest and three keepers of the threshold.
people.seraiah-priest.meaning: Nebuzaradan takes him from Jerusalem and brings him to Riblah. The king of Babylon puts him to death there. He is not Seraiah the Netophathite captain in the same chapter.
people.zephaniah-priest.role: Second priest put to death at Riblah
people.zephaniah-priest.relations: Taken with Seraiah the chief priest to Riblah.
people.zephaniah-priest.meaning: Nebuzaradan takes him with Seraiah the chief priest after Jerusalem falls. He brings them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. The king puts them to death there.
people.gedaliah.meaning: Nebuchadnezzar makes him governor over the people left in Judah. At Mizpah he swears to the captains that serving Babylon will go well. In the seventh month Ishmael and ten men kill him.
people.ishmael-nethaniah.role: Royal family member who kills Gedaliah
people.ishmael-nethaniah.meaning: He comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah with the other captains. In the seventh month he returns with ten men and kills Gedaliah. He also kills the Jews and Chaldeans with him. The people then flee to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans.
people.seraiah-captain.role: Captain who comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
people.seraiah-captain.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the captains to stay and serve the king of Babylon. He is not Seraiah the chief priest.
people.johanan-kareah.role: Captain who comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
people.johanan-kareah.relations: Son of Kareah. He comes to Mizpah with the other captains.
people.johanan-kareah.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the captains to stay and serve the king of Babylon. This book says nothing more about him.
people.jaazaniah.role: Captain who comes to Gedaliah at Mizpah
people.jaazaniah.meaning: He comes with his men to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Gedaliah tells the captains to stay and serve the king of Babylon. This book says nothing more about him.
people.evil-merodach.role: King of Babylon who frees Jehoiachin
people.evil-merodach.relations: King of Babylon in the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin’s captivity. Also known as Amel Marduk.
people.evil-merodach.meaning: In the year he becomes king, he lets Jehoiachin out of prison. He speaks kindly to him and seats him above the other kings in Babylon. He gives him food every day for the rest of his life.
people.ahaziah-ahab.role: King of Israel who sends to Baal Zebub
people.ahaziah-ahab.relations: Son of Ahab. He has no son, so Jehoram rules after him.
people.ahaziah-ahab.meaning: He falls through the lattice of his upper room and is sick. He sends men to ask Baal Zebub, god of Ekron, if he will live. Elijah tells him he will die, and he does. He is not Ahaziah, the later king of Judah.
people.elijah.role: Prophet taken up to heaven by a whirlwind
people.elijah.relations: Called Elijah the Tishbite. Elisha serves him and follows him.
people.elijah.meaning: He tells King Ahaziah he will die. Fire from the sky burns up two captains and their men. He parts the Jordan with his mantle and goes up by a whirlwind. Later Jehu says Elijah’s words about Ahab’s house and Jezebel have come true.
people.elisha.role: Prophet who takes up Elijah’s mantle
people.elisha.relations: Son of Shaphat. He serves Elijah, and Gehazi serves him.
people.elisha.meaning: He sees Elijah taken up and parts the Jordan with his mantle. He helps a widow, raises the Shunammite’s son, and heals Naaman. He warns Israel’s king about Syria and sends a prophet to anoint Jehu. Dying, he tells King Joash he will beat Syria three times.
people.jehoshaphat.role: King of Judah who asks for a prophet
people.jehoshaphat.relations: Son of Asa and Azubah. Father of Jehoram of Judah.
people.jehoshaphat.meaning: He agrees to go with Israel’s king against Moab. When the army has no water, he asks for a prophet of the LORD. Elisha says he helps only because Jehoshaphat is there. His son Jehoram becomes king of Judah.
people.ben-hadad-ahab.role: King of Syria who besieges Samaria
people.ben-hadad-ahab.relations: Hazael serves him, then rules in his place. He is not Hazael’s son Benhadad.
people.ben-hadad-ahab.meaning: He gathers his army and besieges Samaria until the city starves. Later he lies sick in Damascus and sends Hazael to ask Elisha about it. Hazael spreads a wet cloth over his face, and he dies. Chapter 5 does not name the king of Syria who sends Naaman.
people.hazael.role: Syrian king who attacks Israel and Judah
people.hazael.relations: He serves Benhadad, king of Syria, then rules after him. Father of the later Benhadad.
people.hazael.meaning: Elisha weeps and tells him the harm he will do to Israel. Next day he lays a wet cloth on the king’s face, and the king dies. He takes Israel’s land east of the Jordan and crushes Israel under Jehoahaz. He takes Gath, and Joash of Judah pays him to leave Jerusalem.
people.jehu-nimshi.role: Captain anointed king who destroys Ahab’s house
people.jehu-nimshi.relations: Son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, who is not Judah’s king. Father of Jehoahaz of Israel.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: A young prophet anoints him king at Ramoth Gilead. He kills Joram, has Ahaziah of Judah struck, and has Jezebel thrown down. He has Ahab’s seventy sons killed and kills the worshipers of Baal. He keeps the golden calves, and the LORD promises him four generations of kings.
people.naboth.role: Jezreelite whose blood the LORD repays
people.naboth.relations: A man of Jezreel. Jehu meets Joram on his land.
people.naboth.meaning: Naboth is dead before this book begins. Jehu meets Joram and Ahaziah on Naboth’s land. Jehu recalls the LORD’s word that he saw the blood of Naboth and his sons. He has Joram’s body thrown on that same ground.
people.ahab.role: Earlier king of Israel whose house Jehu destroys
people.ahab.relations: Son of Omri and husband of Jezebel. Father of Ahaziah and Joram, kings of Israel.
people.ahab.meaning: Ahab dies before this book begins. Jehoram of Judah marries his daughter and follows his ways. Jehu kills his son Joram and has his seventy sons killed in Samaria. Later Manasseh makes an Asherah as Ahab did.
people.jezebel.role: Ahab’s wife, thrown from a window
people.jezebel.relations: Wife of Ahab and mother of Joram of Israel. Jehu calls her a king’s daughter.
people.jezebel.meaning: The young prophet says the LORD will avenge his prophets’ blood on her. She paints her eyes, looks out the window, and calls Jehu a murderer. Men at the window throw her down at Jehu’s word. Dogs eat her body, as Elijah had said.
people.jeroboam.role: Earlier king of Israel who made golden calves
people.jeroboam.meaning: Jeroboam son of Nebat ruled long before this book. He made the golden calves at Bethel and Dan. The book says king after king of Israel kept his sins. Josiah at last breaks down his altar at Bethel.
people.judah-man-god.role: Unnamed man of God buried at Bethel
people.judah-man-god.relations: He came from Judah. He is buried beside a prophet from Samaria.
people.judah-man-god.meaning: Long before, he spoke against the altar at Bethel. Josiah burns bones on that altar, as the man had said. Josiah sees his tomb and orders that no one move his bones.
people.bethel-old-prophet.role: Unnamed prophet buried with the man of God
people.bethel-old-prophet.relations: The text says he came out of Samaria. He lies in the tomb with the man of God.
people.bethel-old-prophet.meaning: Josiah tells his men to leave the man of God’s bones alone. They also leave this prophet’s bones, which lie with them. This book tells nothing more about him.
people.david.role: Earlier king, the measure for Judah’s kings
people.david.relations: Father of Solomon. The book calls him the father of Judah’s kings.
people.david.meaning: David ruled long before this book. The book measures each king of Judah against him. The LORD spares Judah and defends Jerusalem for David’s sake.
people.solomon.role: Earlier king whose high places Josiah defiles
people.solomon.meaning: Solomon had built high places near Jerusalem for Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom. Josiah defiles them. Babylon later cuts up the gold vessels Solomon made for the temple.
people.moses.role: Earlier leader who gave the law
people.moses.meaning: Moses lived long before this book. Hezekiah breaks the bronze serpent Moses made, because people burned incense to it. The book says Israel fell for not keeping what Moses commanded. It says Josiah turned to the LORD by all the law of Moses.
people.azariah.role: King of Judah who lives apart as a leper
people.azariah.relations: Son of Amaziah and Jecoliah. Father of Jotham.
people.azariah.meaning: The people of Judah make him king at sixteen, and he rules fifty-two years. He builds Elath and restores it to Judah. The LORD strikes him, and he lives as a leper in a separate house. The text calls him both Azariah and Uzziah.
people.jotham.role: King of Judah who builds the upper gate
people.jotham.meaning: He runs the king’s house and judges the people while his father is a leper. He then rules Judah for sixteen years. He builds the upper gate of the LORD’s house. In his days Rezin and Pekah begin to come against Judah.
people.pekah.role: King of Israel who attacks Judah with Rezin
people.pekah.relations: Son of Remaliah. He is Pekahiah’s captain and kills him.
people.pekah.meaning: He kills King Pekahiah and rules Israel for twenty years. Tiglath Pileser takes Gilead, Galilee, and other towns and carries the people away. Pekah and Rezin besiege Ahaz in Jerusalem but cannot beat him. Hoshea kills Pekah and takes the throne.
people.hoshea.relations: Son of Elah. He kills Pekah and rules after him.
people.hoshea.meaning: He kills Pekah and becomes king. He pays tribute to Shalmaneser, then sends to So of Egypt and stops paying. The king of Assyria puts him in prison. Samaria falls after three years, and Israel is carried to Assyria.
people.pul.role: King of Assyria who takes silver and towns
people.pul.relations: Chapter 15 names Pul in verse 19 and Tiglath Pileser in verse 29.
people.pul.meaning: Pul comes against Israel, and Menahem pays him a thousand talents of silver. Tiglath Pileser takes Gilead and Galilee and carries the people to Assyria. Ahaz pays him, and he takes Damascus and kills Rezin. The older manual treats the two names as one king.
people.rezin.role: King of Syria who attacks Judah
people.rezin.relations: King of Syria at Damascus. He fights beside Pekah of Israel.
people.rezin.meaning: He and Pekah besiege Ahaz in Jerusalem but cannot beat him. He takes Elath for Syria and drives out the Jews. Ahaz pays Assyria for help. The king of Assyria takes Damascus and kills Rezin.
people.ahaz.role: King of Judah who pays Assyria for help
people.ahaz.meaning: Rezin and Pekah besiege him, so he sends temple silver and gold to Tiglath Pileser. He sees an altar in Damascus and has Urijah build one like it. He moves the bronze altar and takes apart other temple pieces. He also makes his son pass through the fire.
people.hezekiah.role: King of Judah who prays when Assyria comes
people.hezekiah.meaning: He removes the high places and breaks the bronze serpent. He pays Sennacherib silver and gold, yet an Assyrian army still comes to Jerusalem. He spreads the threatening letter before the LORD and prays. Later he is healed of a deadly sickness and shows Babylon’s men all his treasures.
people.sennacherib.role: King of Assyria who attacks Judah
people.sennacherib.relations: King of Assyria. Father of Esar Haddon, who rules after him.
people.sennacherib.meaning: He takes Judah’s fortified cities and makes Hezekiah pay silver and gold. He sends an army and a letter that mock the LORD. The LORD’s angel strikes his camp, and he goes home to Nineveh and is killed. His royal inscription also records a war in Judah, for a different purpose.
people.rabshakeh.role: Assyrian officer who speaks at Jerusalem’s wall
people.rabshakeh.relations: Sent by Sennacherib with Tartan and Rabsaris.
people.rabshakeh.meaning: He tells Hezekiah’s men that Egypt and the LORD cannot save them. They ask him to speak Syrian, not the Jews’ language. He shouts in the Jews’ language so the people on the wall hear. Rabshakeh is an official title.
people.eliakim.role: Head of Hezekiah’s household who meets Rabshakeh
people.eliakim.relations: Son of Hilkiah, and over the king’s household. He is not Josiah’s son Eliakim, later named Jehoiakim.
people.eliakim.meaning: He goes out with Shebna and Joah to hear Rabshakeh. He asks Rabshakeh to speak Syrian so the people will not understand. He tears his clothes and tells Hezekiah. Hezekiah then sends him to Isaiah.
people.hebna.relations: Named with Eliakim and Joah. The text also spells his name Shebnah.
people.hebna.meaning: He goes out with Eliakim and Joah to hear Rabshakeh. They return to Hezekiah with torn clothes and tell him the words. Hezekiah sends him with Eliakim to Isaiah.
people.joah.meaning: He goes out with Eliakim and Shebna to hear Rabshakeh. They return to Hezekiah with torn clothes and tell him the words.
people.isaiah.meaning: He tells Hezekiah not to fear, because Assyria’s king will go home. He sends the LORD’s word that Sennacherib will not enter Jerusalem. He tells the sick king he will die, then that he has fifteen more years. He warns that Hezekiah’s treasures and some of his sons will go to Babylon.
people.tirhakah.role: King of Ethiopia said to march against Assyria
people.tirhakah.relations: The text calls him king of Ethiopia.
people.tirhakah.meaning: The king of Assyria hears that Tirhakah has come out to fight him. He then sends messengers to Hezekiah again. The text does not say what Tirhakah does.
people.adramelech.role: One of two men who kill Sennacherib
people.adramelech.meaning: He and Sharezer strike Sennacherib with the sword in the house of Nisroch. They escape to the land of Ararat. He is not the god Adrammelech named in 17:31.
people.sharezer.role: One of two men who kill Sennacherib
people.sharezer.meaning: He and Adrammelech strike Sennacherib with the sword in the house of Nisroch. They escape to the land of Ararat. The text says nothing more about him.
people.esarhaddon.relations: Son of Sennacherib. The text spells his name Esar Haddon.
people.esarhaddon.meaning: He becomes king of Assyria after Sennacherib is killed. The text says nothing more about him.
people.merodach-baladan.role: King of Babylon who sends men to Hezekiah
people.merodach-baladan.relations: Son of Baladan. The text here spells his name Berodach Baladan.
people.merodach-baladan.meaning: He hears that Hezekiah has been sick and sends letters and a present. Hezekiah shows his men every treasure. Isaiah then says all of it will be carried to Babylon.
people.manasseh-king.role: King of Judah who rebuilds the high places
people.manasseh-king.meaning: He rebuilds the high places that his father Hezekiah destroyed. He puts altars and an Asherah in the LORD’s house and sheds much innocent blood. The prophets say the LORD will wipe Jerusalem like a dish. The book later says Judah falls for his sins.
people.josiah.role: King of Judah who acts on the book of the law
people.josiah.relations: Son of Amon and Jedidah. Father of Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah.
people.josiah.meaning: He becomes king at eight. He hears the book of the law, tears his clothes, and sends men to Huldah. He makes a covenant, clears out the idols and high places, and keeps the Passover. Pharaoh Necoh kills him at Megiddo.
people.necho.role: King of Egypt who kills Josiah
people.necho.relations: King of Egypt. The text spells his name Necoh.
people.necho.meaning: He marches toward the river Euphrates, and he kills Josiah at Megiddo. He binds Jehoahaz at Riblah and takes him to Egypt. He makes Eliakim king, renames him Jehoiakim, and demands silver and gold from Judah.
people.jehoiakim.role: King of Judah set up by Egypt
people.jehoiakim.relations: Son of Josiah and Zebidah, first named Eliakim. Father of Jehoiachin.
people.jehoiakim.meaning: Pharaoh Necoh makes him king and changes his name from Eliakim. He taxes the people of the land to pay Pharaoh. He serves Nebuchadnezzar for three years and then rebels. Raiding bands then come against Judah.
people.jehoiachin.role: King of Judah taken to Babylon
people.jehoiachin.meaning: He rules three months. He goes out to Nebuchadnezzar with his mother and officers and is taken to Babylon. In his thirty-seventh year there, Evilmerodach frees him from prison. He eats before the king every day for the rest of his life.
people.zedekiah.relations: Son of Josiah and Hamutal, first named Mattaniah. Uncle of Jehoiachin.
people.zedekiah.meaning: The king of Babylon makes him king and changes his name. He rebels, and Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem until the bread is gone. He flees by night and is caught in the plains of Jericho. At Riblah they kill his sons before him, blind him, and take him to Babylon.
people.nebuchadnezzar.role: King of Babylon who conquers Judah
people.nebuchadnezzar.relations: King of Babylon. Nebuzaradan is the captain of his guard.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: He makes Jehoiakim his servant. He takes Jehoiachin, the treasures, and ten thousand captives to Babylon. He makes Zedekiah king, then besieges Jerusalem when Zedekiah rebels. At Riblah he judges Zedekiah and puts Judah’s leaders to death.
people.nebuzaradan.meaning: He burns the LORD’s house, the king’s house, and every great house in Jerusalem. He carries away the people left in the city. He leaves some of the poorest to work the vineyards and fields. He takes the chief priests and officers to Riblah.
places.aphek.summary: In chapter 13 Elisha tells King Joash he will strike the Syrians in Aphek.
places.aphek.limits: The place of this battle is not certain. The marker shows a general location.
places.assyria.summary: Assyria’s kings take tribute from Israel and Judah. In chapter 17 they carry Israel away to Assyria.
places.assyria.limits: Assyria is a wide region. The marker shows only its general location.
places.babylon.summary: In chapter 20 men from Babylon visit Hezekiah. In chapters 24 and 25 Nebuchadnezzar carries Judah’s kings and people there.
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the general location of the city and its land.
places.beth-shemesh.summary: In chapter 14 Joash of Israel defeats and captures Amaziah of Judah at Beth Shemesh.
places.beth-shemesh.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.bethel.summary: In chapter 2 Elijah and Elisha stop at Bethel, and youths mock Elisha there. In chapter 23 Josiah breaks down Jeroboam’s altar.
places.bethel.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.carmel.summary: In chapter 2 Elisha goes to Mount Carmel. In chapter 4 the Shunammite woman rides there to find him.
places.carmel.limits: The text does not say where on the mountain Elisha stays. The marker is general.
places.damascus.summary: In chapter 8 Elisha visits Damascus, where Benhadad lies sick. In chapter 16 Assyria takes the city, and Ahaz sees an altar there.
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.dothan.summary: In chapter 6 a Syrian army surrounds Elisha at Dothan. His servant sees horses and chariots of fire.
places.dothan.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.edom.summary: In chapter 3 the king of Edom joins the war on Moab. In chapter 8 Edom breaks free of Judah. In chapter 14 Amaziah kills ten thousand Edomites.
places.edom.limits: Edom is a wide region. The marker shows only its general location.
places.egypt.summary: In chapter 17 Hoshea sends messengers to So, king of Egypt. In chapter 23 Pharaoh Necoh takes Jehoahaz there. In chapter 25 the people flee to Egypt.
places.egypt.limits: Egypt is a wide land. The marker shows only its general location.
places.ekron.summary: In chapter 1 Ahaziah sends messengers to ask Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron.
places.ekron.limits: The marker shows the town, not a confirmed temple site.
places.elath.summary: In chapter 14 Azariah builds Elath and restores it to Judah. In chapter 16 Rezin takes it for Syria.
places.elath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.galilee.summary: In chapter 15 Tiglath Pileser takes Galilee and carries its people to Assyria.
places.galilee.limits: Galilee is a region. The marker shows only its general location.
places.gath.summary: In chapter 12 Hazael, king of Syria, fights against Gath and takes it.
places.gath.limits: The marker shows a general location. The exact site is not certain.
places.gath-hepher.summary: Chapter 14 names Gath Hepher as the home of Jonah the prophet.
places.gath-hepher.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.gilead.summary: In chapter 10 Hazael takes Gilead from Israel. In chapter 15 Tiglath Pileser takes it and carries the people away.
places.gilead.limits: Gilead is a wide region east of the Jordan. The marker shows its general location.
places.gur.summary: In chapter 9 Jehu’s men strike Ahaziah of Judah at the ascent of Gur. The text places it by Ibleam.
places.gur.limits: The exact place of the ascent is not known. The marker is general.
places.jericho.summary: In chapter 2 Elisha heals Jericho’s bad water with salt. In chapter 25 the Chaldeans catch Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jerusalem.summary: Judah’s kings rule from Jerusalem. Assyria threatens it in chapters 18 and 19. In chapter 25 Babylon burns the temple and houses and breaks down the walls.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.jezreel.summary: In chapter 9 Jehu kills Joram at Jezreel, and Jezebel is thrown from a window. In chapter 10 the heads of Ahab’s sons are sent there.
places.jezreel.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jordan.summary: In chapter 2 Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan on dry ground. In chapter 5 Naaman dips in it seven times. In chapter 6 an ax head floats there.
places.jordan.limits: The text does not say where on the river each event happens. The marker is general.
places.kir-hareseth.summary: In chapter 3 the armies of Israel, Judah, and Edom attack Kir Hareseth. Mesha offers his son on the wall.
places.kir-hareseth.limits: The marker follows a traditional site for the town. The site is not certain.
places.lachish.summary: In chapter 14 Amaziah flees to Lachish and is killed there. In chapter 18 Hezekiah sends word to Sennacherib at Lachish.
places.lachish.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.libnah.summary: In chapter 8 Libnah revolts against Judah. In chapter 19 the king of Assyria fights against it.
places.libnah.limits: Scholars dispute where ancient Libnah was. The marker shows a general area.
places.megiddo.summary: In chapter 9 Ahaziah of Judah flees to Megiddo and dies. In chapter 23 Pharaoh Necoh kills Josiah there.
places.megiddo.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.mizpah.summary: In chapter 25 the captains come to Gedaliah at Mizpah. Ishmael kills him there.
places.mizpah.limits: The site of this Mizpah is not certain. The marker is general.
places.moab.summary: In chapter 3 Moab rebels against Israel, and three kings march against it.
places.moab.limits: Moab is a wide region. The marker shows only its general location.
places.nineveh.summary: In chapter 19 Sennacherib goes home and lives at Nineveh. He is later killed while he worships his god Nisroch.
places.nineveh.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.ramoth-gilead.summary: In chapter 8 Joram is wounded fighting Syria at Ramoth Gilead. In chapter 9 a young prophet anoints Jehu there.
places.ramoth-gilead.limits: The site of Ramoth Gilead is disputed. The marker shows a general area.
places.riblah.summary: In chapter 23 Pharaoh Necoh binds Jehoahaz at Riblah. In chapter 25 Nebuchadnezzar judges Zedekiah there and puts Judah’s leaders to death.
places.riblah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.samaria.summary: Israel’s kings rule from Samaria. Syria besieges it in chapters 6 and 7. In chapter 17 Assyria takes it after three years and carries Israel away.
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.shunem.summary: In chapter 4 a woman of Shunem makes a room for Elisha. Her son dies there, and Elisha brings him back to life.
places.shunem.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
places.tirzah.summary: In chapter 15 Menahem goes up from Tirzah to Samaria and kills Shallum.
places.tirzah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the town.
sources.web.limits: The text alone does not confirm dates, looks, private motives, numbers, or every event.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Map positions are display estimates. A town marker does not confirm each event.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.hayes-kings.limits: A critical literary reading does not confirm the miracles. The lecture shortens the line of kings. Kings itself places Amon before Josiah.
sources.millard-hezekiah.limits: This is one scholar’s argument, not a view all scholars share. Weigh the Assyrian king’s claims and the Bible’s religious claims separately. The article does not confirm the Bible’s death total.
sources.mcclellan-kings.summary: McClellan links Naaman’s request for soil with worship tied to a land. He reads the wrath in Moab as the act of a god.
sources.mcclellan-kings.limits: This is one reading from an older thesis, not an agreed view. The wrath verse does not name Chemosh. The complete thesis and the cited commentaries were not read.
sources.nelson-record.summary: The edition record identifies Nelson’s commentary. The commentary treats Kings as writing about God and faith.
sources.wiki-2-kings.summary: The article gives a broad outline from the kings to the exile. It also lists books for further study.
sources.wiki-2-kings.limits: Use it for background and for finding sources only. Its claims about the scroll and the exile are checked against scripture and scholarly sources.
sources.lds-northern-fall.limits: Church application does not by itself settle dates or campaign numbers. Proposed motives and exact sites are not adopted.
chapters.*.mapNote: Points show the towns and regions the chapter names. Some sites are proposed or disputed, so positions are approximate.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Lines join the places in the order the chapter names them. The real roads and army paths are not known.
